en.title: The Odyssey Just Sailed Past $1 Billion, Becoming Nolan's Biggest Hit
en.summary: Christopher Nolan's epic journey has officially crossed the monumental billion-dollar box office mark. This cinematic feat makes it the director's highest-grossing film to date.
en.body:
Christopher Nolan's ambitious retelling of **The Odyssey** has officially surpassed $1 billion at the global box office, cementing its place as the director's most financially successful film ever. This monumental achievement also marks it as the fifth film of 2026 to reach this coveted benchmark, a testament to its widespread appeal. The epic, starring **Matt Damon**, has been on a remarkable trajectory since its release, outpacing many expectations and now stands as a titan in Nolan's impressive filmography. It's a significant moment, especially considering it's the first time Nolan has hit this mark without featuring a Caped Crusader.

While **The Odyssey** is soaring, it's facing stiff competition. **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** has already crossed the $1.1 billion mark and is expected to hold onto the top spot for the weekend. This dynamic has sparked conversations among fans and industry watchers about the box office dominance of stars like **Tom Holland** and **Zendaya**, who appear in both films. For **Zendaya**, this year has been particularly strong, with her roles in **The Odyssey**, **Spider-Man: Brand New Day**, and the earlier success of **The Drama** ($135 million) contributing to a banner year. However, the ultimate box office record still belongs to **Zoe Saldaña**, thanks to her extensive work in massive franchises like *Avatar*, *Avengers*, *Pirates of the Caribbean*, and *Star Trek*.

## A New Benchmark for Nolan

The success of **The Odyssey** is particularly striking given its R-rating and its complex narrative. Reaching $900 million faster than any other 2026 film that ultimately crossed the billion-dollar threshold is a significant record in itself. This performance solidifies Nolan's reputation as a filmmaker who can deliver challenging, thought-provoking cinema that also achieves massive commercial success. The film's journey to the billion-dollar mark is a story of strategic release, critical acclaim, and a powerful audience connection to its grand themes and stunning visuals.

## The Star Power Play

This box office battle highlights the immense drawing power of established franchises and beloved stars. **The Odyssey**'s success, alongside **Spider-Man: Brand New Day**, demonstrates a continued audience appetite for large-scale cinematic experiences. For fans invested in the careers of **Holland** and **Zendaya**, tracking their box office performance across different films offers an exciting meta-narrative. While neither may surpass **Holland**'s 2019 performance in *Avengers: Endgame* and *Spider-Man: Far From Home*, their 2026 efforts are undeniably impressive and have made a significant impact on the year's box office landscape.

## What's Next

With **The Odyssey** now firmly in the billion-dollar club and **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** leading the pack, all eyes are on the final box office tallies for the year. Fans can look forward to potential home release announcements for **The Odyssey** and continued speculation about Nolan's next project. The success also bodes well for **Zendaya**'s upcoming role in the third installment of Denis Villeneuve's acclaimed sci-fi series.

content_raw: Odysseus might be a complicated man, but the money ain’t:  Deadline  reports today that Christopher Nolan’s  The Odyssey   has just crossed the billion-dollar mark at the box office, becoming the fifth movie of 2026 to do so to date. (It’s the third of Nolan’s movies to hit the benchmark, meanwhile, and the first to do so while not featuring a Batted Man.) Although harder preview numbers aren’t in yet, the Matt Damon-starring epic is actually expected to become the highest-grossing film of Nolan’s whole career at some point over this weekend, beating out 2008’s The Dark Knight —which is wild, considering that it’s also expected to lose the weekend box office, to Spider-Man: Brand New Day , by a pretty comfortable The A.V. Club ‘s Slack channels on Friday afternoon, where we—as occasionally susceptible to silly games with movie numbers as anybody else—tried to work out whether either member of Hollywood power couple Tom Holland and Zendaya, who both appear in both films, was about to have the biggest box office year of all time. (Nobody’s touching Zoe Saldaña for the overall record, meanwhile ; that’s the power of all those Avatar ,  Avengers ,  Pirates , and Star Trek  movies.) Neither Holland nor Zendaya is likely to top the one-two punch Holland landed back in 2019, when he appeared in both  Spider-Man: Far From Home  and biggest-all-timer  Avengers: Endgame . But Zendaya is giving her new husband a pretty decent run for the studios’ money: Besides Odyssey  and  Brand New Day , she had  The Drama   earlier this year, which brought in a tidy $135 million, and will star in the third installment in Denis Villeneuve’s highly lucrative Dune  franchise before the year is out.  And while we’re playing these ultimately meaning-light games with numbers, it’s worth noting that, for those who use the billion mark as a barometer of Hollywood’s box office health, 2026 is in pretty damn good shape. Five—which is almost guaranteed to become at least six before the year is out, courtesy of  Avengers: Doomsday —is already the most movies to clear the bar since the COVID-19 lockdowns. And while 2026 might not end up breaking the record 8 movies that did so in 2019—a year where movie audiences were going so nuts they were giving, like, Aladdin  a billion bucks—the year is still on track to beat every other year on record on that score.
